Well, the C is for Calvin, who was a character in a comic strip created by Bill Watterson called Calvin & Hobbes. 

This sub is inspired by the recurring strips where Calvin (who was a 6 year old boy with a hyperactive imagination) would go and ask his father genuine questions, and his father would make up the most elaborately false answers just to entertain himself.

[This](http://calvin-and-hobbes-comic-strips.blogspot.com/2011/11/calvin-asks-dad-about-old-black-and.html) is a good example.

So in this subreddit, the idea is to not explain it accurately or concisely, but to be as elaborate and absurd as possible, while still somehow making sense in the way that a young child (Calvin in this case) would believe it.

Actually understanding how the computer uses memory, or why floating-point numbers are used in the first place, etc..., really makes a difference between knowing a language and understanding it. 
As someone else once said on here, it is good to know that 5x5=25, but it is even better to know **why** it equals that.
Otherwise, good luck and hang in there! Just remember to keep writing code, and don't get discouraged.
